questions.title: Strategic Alignment
questions.text: How effectively does your awareness program align with organizational risk management goals and compliance standards?

options.label: No documented alignment with risk management goals or compliance standards
Awareness program mentions risk management but lacks integration or compliance alignment
Program partially aligns with risk management goals and references compliance frameworks informally
Program is explicitly aligned with organizational risks and compliance standards; reviewed periodically
Fully integrated with risk management and compliance, with regular updates based on evolving threats and requirements

questions.title: Governance Documentation
questions.text: How well is your program documented and aligned with internal policies and external compliance requirements?

options.label: No documentation or alignment with internal or external requirements
Minimal documentation exists but lacks alignment with compliance standards
Program is documented and partially aligned with policies; limited reference to compliance requirements
Comprehensive documentation exists, aligning with policies and most compliance requirements
Fully documented, consistently aligned with all policies and compliance standards; reviewed annually or as regulations change

questions.title: Executive Support
questions.text: How strong is the executive support and funding for the awareness program?

options.label: No executive support or dedicated funding for the program
Minimal executive awareness; limited or inconsistent funding
Some executive buy-in and a modest budget; funding is not yet prioritized
Strong executive advocacy and a dedicated budget that supports program goals
Executive leadership champions the program with robust, sustained funding tied to strategic priorities

questions.title: Continuous Improvement
questions.text: How frequently does the organization conduct comprehensive assessments of its security posture, including awareness program impacts?

options.label: No formal assessment of the security posture or awareness program
Occasional assessments, but they are informal and lack actionable insights
Assessments occur annually, with some focus on awareness program impacts
Regular, structured assessments that include the program's role in overall security posture
Frequent and thorough assessments integrating awareness program outcomes into broader security reviews

questions.title: Risk vs. Compliance Alignment
questions.text: Does your awareness program align primarily with compliance requirements or organizational risk management priorities?

options.label: Program is entirely compliance-driven with no organizational risk considerations
Strong compliance alignment but limited integration with organizational risk management
Balanced approach addressing both compliance and some organizational risk priorities
Program is risk-informed with compliance as a component; aligns with organizational risk strategy
Fully integrated with enterprise risk management; threat-informed and risk-prioritized with compliance embedded

questions.title: Threat-Informed Training
questions.text: How does your program incorporate real-world threat intelligence and actual security incidents into training content?

options.label: No incorporation of threat intelligence or actual incidents; training is entirely generic
Occasional mention of recent major incidents but no systematic threat integration
Some incorporation of threat data; periodic updates based on notable incidents
Regular integration of threat intelligence and incident data into training content and simulations
Continuous, automated integration of threat intelligence with real-time adaptation of training to emerging threats

questions.title: Targeted Communication
questions.text: Are awareness efforts designed to target specific employee groups or personas?

options.label: No efforts are made to tailor engagement to specific employee groups
Minimal customization; general awareness efforts apply broadly to all employees
Some tailoring for key employee groups (e.g., high-risk roles) but inconsistent application
Engagement efforts are tailored to multiple personas and aligned with their roles and risks
Fully personalized engagement strategies are embedded, regularly updated, and supported by employee feedback

questions.title: Active Participation
questions.text: Are there meaningful rewards or recognition programs to encourage participation?

options.label: No incentives or motivation strategies are in place
Minimal or ad hoc rewards exist but lack structure or effectiveness
Some structured incentives exist but are limited in scope or reach
Incentive programs are well-structured, accessible, and encourage widespread participation
Incentive programs are dynamic, engaging, and integrated into the organizational culture to sustain long-term participation

questions.title: Communication Strategy
questions.text: Are communication strategies effective in reaching all levels of the organization?

options.label: No defined communication strategy; awareness efforts are sporadic
Basic communication occurs but lacks consistency or reach
Communication strategies are structured but may not effectively reach all organizational levels
Communication strategies are well-defined, consistent, and reach most employees effectively
Communication is strategic, inclusive, and seamlessly integrates into organizational workflows to maximize reach and impact

questions.title: Cultural Relevance
questions.text: Do your awareness efforts reflect the cultural values and language preferences of your workforce?

options.label: Awareness efforts do not consider cultural or language differences
Some basic adjustments are made but lack depth or relevance to cultural values
Efforts include basic cultural and language considerations for some employee groups
Awareness initiatives are thoughtfully aligned with cultural values and language preferences across the workforce
Fully tailored awareness efforts are integrated, with regular updates based on employee feedback and demographic shifts

questions.title: Feedback Responsiveness
questions.text: Are employees able to provide feedback on the effectiveness of engagement strategies?

options.label: No feedback mechanisms are available for employees
Basic feedback mechanisms exist but are rarely used or reviewed
Feedback is occasionally collected but not systematically used to improve engagement
Feedback mechanisms are well-established and regularly inform engagement strategies
Feedback is consistently collected, analyzed, and integrated into continuous improvements, fostering a collaborative culture

questions.title: Performance Measurement
questions.text: How effectively does the program use metrics to track progress and demonstrate impact?

options.label: No metrics are used to track progress or demonstrate impact
Limited metrics are collected, but they are inconsistently applied
Metrics are tracked but focus on basic outcomes like training completion rates
A range of meaningful metrics is tracked and used for program adjustments
Metrics are comprehensive, data-driven, and used to drive decision-making and continuous improvement

questions.title: Simulation Effectiveness
questions.text: How realistic are your phishing simulations compared to actual threats your organization faces?

options.label: No phishing simulation program in place
Basic generic simulations with no connection to real threats; simple click tracking only
Moderate realism with some variety; basic consequence pages but limited connection to actual threats
Advanced simulations reflecting common threat patterns; realistic consequence modeling with coaching
Sophisticated threat-actor-based simulations mirroring actual attacks received; comprehensive consequence modeling with personalized follow-up

questions.title: Maturity Evaluation
questions.text: Does your organization regularly conduct self-assessments to evaluate program maturity?

options.label: No self-assessments are conducted
Rare or informal self-assessments are conducted without actionable insights
Structured self-assessments occur annually but focus on limited aspects of program maturity
Comprehensive self-assessments occur regularly and inform program improvements
Self-assessments are dynamic, leveraging data-driven insights to drive continuous improvement and benchmark progress

questions.title: Risk-Driven Assessment
questions.text: Are risks and vulnerabilities regularly assessed and used to guide program improvements?

options.label: Risks and vulnerabilities are not assessed or used for improvement
Risks are occasionally assessed but lack integration into program updates
Risk assessments occur regularly but are not consistently applied to program adjustments
Risk-based metrics are routinely used to guide program updates and prioritize initiatives
Risk-based metrics are fully integrated into a proactive strategy for continuous improvement and adaptation

questions.title: KPIs and Reporting
questions.text: Are key performance indicators tracked through accessible dashboards or reports?

options.label: No KPIs or dashboards are in use
Basic KPIs are tracked but lack actionable reporting or visibility
KPIs are tracked and reported but lack advanced visualization or comprehensive insights
Dashboards are well-designed, accessible, and provide actionable insights to stakeholders
KPIs and dashboards are fully integrated into decision-making processes, offering advanced analytics and predictive capabilities

questions.title: Relevant, Tailored Training
questions.text: Are training materials aligned with identified risks and tailored to employee needs?

options.label: No formal training materials are in place
Basic training materials exist but lack alignment with specific risks or employee needs
Training materials are somewhat tailored and address general risks but lack depth
Training materials are well-designed, risk-aligned, and tailored to different employee roles
Training is fully customized, continuously updated, and aligned with specific risks and organizational priorities

questions.title: Effective Learning Methods
questions.text: Are phishing simulations realistic, engaging, and used as an educational tool?

options.label: No phishing simulations are conducted
Occasional simulations are conducted but lack realism or educational follow-up
Simulations are regularly conducted but focus primarily on testing, with limited education
Simulations are engaging, realistic, and integrated with training for behavioral improvement
Simulations are dynamic, fully customized, and used as a core educational tool with measurable results

questions.title: Accessible, Inclusive Training
questions.text: Are training materials inclusive, multilingual, and easy for employees to access?

options.label: Training materials are not accessible or inclusive
Limited accessibility, with minimal language options or inclusivity considerations
Some accessibility features exist, but language and inclusivity efforts are inconsistent
Training materials are inclusive, available in multiple languages, and accessible to most employees
Fully accessible and inclusive training, covering a wide range of languages and formats to ensure global reach

questions.title: Flexible, Effective Delivery
questions.text: Is there a clear cadence for delivering training to employees?

options.label: No formal training schedule exists
Training is delivered sporadically, without a consistent schedule
A basic schedule exists, but training is infrequent or inconsistent
Training is delivered regularly, with a well-defined cadence (e.g., quarterly)
Training frequency is strategically planned, adaptive to organizational needs, and seamlessly integrated into workflows

questions.title: Integrated Training Lifecycle
questions.text: Is training integrated into onboarding and professional development plans?

options.label: Training is not integrated into onboarding or professional development
Training is occasionally included in onboarding but not professional development
Training is included in onboarding but inconsistently integrated into ongoing development plans
Training is systematically included in onboarding and professional development plans
Training is fully integrated into onboarding, continuous learning, and career development, ensuring sustained awareness
